decisions.reason: As a flagship product close to the firm's core dosimetry and QA capabilities, it fits strongly with existing knowledge and is therefore very likely to be retained and improved rather than withdrawn.
This oncology risk-management software builds on the firm's established software and clinical QA competences, so the firm is well placed to learn from early use and keep developing it.
The CT image quality test phantom extends the firm's existing imaging and QA offer, and in an expanding R&D-active firm that makes continued commercialization more likely than exit.

Because the mammography image quality phantom is more distant from the firm's main knowledge base, absorptive-capacity logic implies a noticeably higher withdrawal risk, but the firm's broad range and research links still make retention somewhat more likely.

This full field mammography test phantom is also relatively distant from the core radiation-therapy QA base, so it faces elevated risk, though the firm's strong technical resources and expansion suggest it will probably get more time on the market.

As a flagship multi-model imaging QA line that builds on established capabilities, it aligns well with the firm's direction of integration, measurement, and automation and is unlikely to be dropped soon.
